newsitem.title: USA: Diana adopts stockholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Diana adopts stockholder rights plan.

text.p: Diana Corp said Thursday its directors adopted a stockholder rights plan designed to enable all stockholders to realize the long term value of their investments.
Diana said it declared a dividend of one right on each outstanding share of Diana common stock, payable September 16, 1996 to stockholders of record the same date.
The company said the rights would be triggered if a person or group acquires 15 percent or more of Diana's common stock.

"The rights plan is not intended to and will not prevent a takeover of Diana at a full and fair price and it will not restrict consideration by Diana's board of directors of any offer on terms favorable to all stockholders," said Richard Fisher, chairman and president.
"It is intended to protect the interests of stockholders in the event the company is confronted with coercive or unfair takeover tactics," he said in a statement.

The rights plan does not weaken Diana's financial strength or interfere with its business plans, he said. The issuance of the rights has no dilutive effect, will not affect reported earnings per share, is not taxable to Diana or its stockholders and will not change the way in which the company's shares are traded, he said.
